body:
Hi Shannon,

You are on the preview list for our Fall Layering Event, so you get early access before the public launch. Through the end of the week, members can browse the newest wool throws, linen shams, pendant lights, woven storage baskets, and tabletop pieces before they appear in the main catalog. Nothing is required from you; this is simply the full announcement with the usual fine print and links in case you want to browse later.

Highlights from the preview:
- 20% off sitewide through Friday at midnight ET
- Free shipping over $75 in the continental U.S.
- New colors added to the Rowan, Mercer, and Vale lines
- Gift receipts now available at checkout
- Members can combine this event with unused birthday rewards
- Early-access window closes Friday, 31 July at 23:59 ET

A few exclusions apply. Custom upholstery, made-to-order lighting, gift cards, and previous purchases are not eligible for price adjustments. Inventory varies by location, and items in your cart are not reserved until checkout is complete. If an item sells out during the preview, we will note expected restock dates on the product page rather than issuing a rain check. Price adjustments on orders placed before the preview opened are handled by the standard fourteen-day policy and are not extended by this event.

A note on shipping: carriers are running one to two days behind in the Northeast because of the heat advisory, so the free-shipping estimate assumes a Monday handoff. Expedited options are still available at checkout for an additional charge, and in-store pickup remains same-day at the Brooklyn and Hudson locations. Made-to-order lighting continues to quote six to eight weeks regardless of the shipping method you choose.

Returns during the preview follow the usual terms. Unused items in original packaging can go back within thirty days for a full refund, and textiles that have been washed are eligible for store credit only. Custom upholstery remains final sale. If a piece arrives damaged, photograph the carton before unpacking and our support team can file the carrier claim on your behalf.

We are also piloting a small repair service at the Brooklyn store for wool goods bought from us in the last three years. There is no signup and no cost estimate to request yet; we will announce details in a later message once the pilot has run through the fall. The idea came out of the number of throws people bring in with a single pulled seam, which is a twenty-minute fix that most tailors will not take on because the piece is not worth their minimum charge.

On the new colors, a word about how they photograph. The Rowan line picked up a deep olive and a muted rust this season, and both read warmer on a screen than they do in daylight. If you are matching to something you already own, the swatch cards are free at either store and we will mail one on request. The Mercer additions are two neutrals that are close enough to each other that we have had returns from people who ordered the wrong one, so the same advice applies there.

The Vale pendant lights are the piece most likely to sell out during the preview. We ordered conservatively because the last run had a lead-time problem at the glassworks, and we would rather be short than promise a December delivery we cannot make. If the finish you want is gone, the product page will show a restock estimate, and those estimates have been accurate within about two weeks this year.

Finally, a note for anyone who bought during the spring event. The birthday reward that went out in April was originally set to expire at the end of July. We have extended those to the end of August so they can be combined with this event rather than wasted against it. Nothing is required to claim the extension; it is already applied to the account.

If you would rather not receive these notices, you can unsubscribe from the list below. Offer terms, exclusions, and return policy details are available at the link in the footer. This email was sent by Orchard & Loom, 88 Mercer St, Brooklyn, NY 11222. To manage preferences, visit the email preferences page or reply to this message if you have trouble with the unsubscribe link.

body:
Dear Cedar Table member,

The summer pairing guide is ready, with menu notes for the bottles in last month's club shipment. This edition covers grilled peaches with the Chenin Blanc, smoked eggplant with the Garnacha, and a chilled red option for outdoor dinners. The guide is informational and does not change your subscription, shipment schedule, or billing date.

A little on where these bottles came from. The Chenin is from a cooperative in the Loire that we have worked with for four years; the 2024 harvest came in early and the wine is noticeably leaner than the vintage you had last summer, which is why the guide leans toward stone fruit rather than the richer pairings we suggested before. The Garnacha is a first-time producer for us, farmed at altitude in Aragon, and it is the bottle our staff argued about most in the tasting panel. Two of us wanted it in the summer box and two thought it belonged in the fall allocation. Summer won.

If you are planning ahead, the September allocation will be announced in late August. Members can pause or change bottle counts from the account page, but nothing is due today. Changes made before the announcement always apply to the next unshipped box, so there is no deadline to watch and no need to time it carefully.

We are also hosting a tasting on Sunday, 9 August at the Hudson shop, and a separate invitation will go out with RSVP details for anyone who wants to attend. That invitation will be the one asking for a response; this message is not it. The tasting is free for club members and twenty dollars for guests, and we will pour the September candidates alongside two bottles that did not make the cut so you can taste the comparison the panel was arguing about.

The tasting itself is worth a paragraph because people ask the same questions every time. It runs from 14:00 to 16:00 ET, it is standing rather than seated, and there is food, though not enough to count as a meal. We pour six wines in flights of two so you can taste them against each other rather than in isolation, which is the whole point of the format. Spitting is normal and nobody will think anything of it. If you are driving, the walk from the lot is about four minutes and there is no charge for parking on Sundays.

We are also changing how the September allocation works, and we would rather flag it now than have it land as a surprise in the announcement. Previously the box was fixed and members swapped bottles afterward, which generated a lot of shipping in both directions. From September the allocation page will open for four days before the box ships, and you can swap up to two bottles during that window at no cost. After the window closes the box is locked. This is not something you need to act on now; the announcement in late August will have the dates and a link.

A housekeeping item: our carrier now requires an adult signature on all wine deliveries in your state. If you have a delivery instruction on file asking us to leave boxes at the door, the carrier will disregard it and hold the box at their depot for five business days. Nothing to change on your end unless you would rather redirect shipments to a work address.

As always, inventory is limited and tasting notes reflect the producer's release notes plus our own staff recommendations. Please drink responsibly. This email was sent because you joined the Cedar Table club list.

Good morning,

July is ending hot, so our nursery team put together a short care note for balcony herbs, citrus trees, and container tomatoes. Water early, skip midday pruning, and move shallow pots out of reflected afternoon heat when possible. These tips are general recommendations, not a notice about any order or service appointment.

The heat advisory is the main thing driving this note. Containers on a south-facing balcony can hit soil temperatures well above what the same plant would see in the ground, and the usual symptom is leaf curl that looks like disease but is only heat stress. Watering twice a day is usually worse than watering deeply once at dawn, because shallow frequent watering keeps roots near the surface where the heat is. If a pot has gone completely dry and water runs straight through, set it in a tray for twenty minutes so the soil can rewet from below.

This weekend we will have discounted terracotta, fresh basil starts, and a small restock of self-watering planters. The sale runs in store only from Friday through Sunday while inventory lasts. Loyalty members can show their phone number at checkout for the usual points, but there is no coupon to activate and no reply needed.

If you recently purchased a Meyer lemon tree, the yellowing leaves described in the guide are common during heat waves and usually resolve on their own once nights drop below 21C. Bring photos to the counter if you want advice next time you visit; the nursery staff are in daily from 09:00 to 17:00 ET and there is no appointment system.

Hi Shannon,

We released a faster receipt search experience in PocketLedger. You can now filter by merchant, card ending, reimbursement status, and tax category from the same screen. Saved searches will roll out next month after we finish testing export behavior with larger teams.

No action is required from account admins. Your workspace settings, connected cards, and reimbursement policy remain the same. The new search tools are available the next time you sign in, and older receipts have already been indexed. If something looks off, our support team can inspect the receipt ID from the help menu.

What changed under the hood, for anyone who cares: search used to run against the receipt text only after a nightly job finished, which is why a receipt uploaded in the afternoon was often not findable until the next morning. Indexing is now incremental, so a receipt is searchable within about thirty seconds of upload. The tradeoff is that the merchant name on a very fresh receipt may be the raw card-network string until our normalizer catches up, usually within a few minutes. Filters that depend on tax category will show the receipt as uncategorized during that window rather than hiding it.

We also reworked how multi-currency receipts display. The amount shown in list view is now the workspace's reporting currency with the original amount underneath, rather than the other way around. Historical reports are unaffected because they were always generated in the reporting currency; only the on-screen list changed.

A few smaller items in this release. CSV export now includes the reimbursement status column that several workspaces had been reconstructing by hand. The mobile app picked up accessibility fixes for screen-reader labels on the capture screen and better contrast on the status chips. And the help menu now surfaces the receipt ID directly, so you no longer have to open the browser console to find it when writing to support.

Known issue: workspaces with more than fifty thousand receipts may see the first search after sign-in take a few seconds while the index warms. We expect to have that resolved in the next release and no configuration change is needed on your side.

You are receiving this because your workspace enabled product announcements.
